questions.prompt: You tuned thresholds on seeds 0-99 and then report the success rate on seeds 0-99. What is wrong?
options: Nothing is wrong, because 100 episodes is already enough for a narrow interval.
The interval should use a normal approximation instead of Wilson.
Tuning saw those seeds, so the rate is optimistic; use unseen seeds.
The seeds are too few; always use at least 10 000 episodes.
questions.explanation: Tuning absorbs the quirks of the seeds it saw. Only unseen seeds give an unbiased estimate.

questions.prompt: 27 successes in 30 episodes. Lower end of the Wilson 95 % interval (give a number between 0 and 1).
questions.explanation: Wilson lower bound for 27/30 is about 0.744.

questions.prompt: In a paired McNemar test on the same 30 seeds, which seeds carry the information?
options: Seeds where exactly one condition succeeded.
All seeds, each weighted by its episode duration in seconds.
Only the seeds where both conditions succeeded.
Only the seeds where both conditions failed.
questions.explanation: Concordant seeds (both ok or both failed) say nothing about which condition is better; only discordant seeds count.

questions.prompt: Discordant seeds: nominal won 9, the ablation won 1 (b=9, c=1). Exact two-sided McNemar p-value.
40 % of your failed episodes are labelled OTHER. What does that mean for the error budget?
options: It is fine: OTHER is a legitimate root cause, so fix it first and move on.
Delete those episodes from the log so the rate improves.
Rename OTHER to NAV_TIMEOUT, the most common cause in practice.
Taxonomy or logging too thin; replay to split OTHER.
questions.explanation: A budget that says OTHER cannot direct work; improve the logging or the categories.

questions.prompt: While recalibrating against the sealed twin you are tempted to open models/corebot_real.xml to read the true wheel radius. Why is that wrong?
options: The file is stored in a binary format and cannot be parsed by hand anyway.
It becomes an answer key; the gain says nothing about sim-to-real.
It breaks MuJoCo determinism for later seeds.
It is allowed as long as you also run step tests afterwards.
questions.explanation: On a real robot you can only run experiments. Reading the parameters destroys the point of the twin.

questions.prompt: Describe how you would pre-register the four ablations of CAP08 before running them.
rubric: States for each ablation a hypothesis with a predicted direction and rough size.
Fixes seeds, n per ablation and the test (paired exact McNemar) before running.
Names the correction for multiple comparisons (Holm) and the number of tests.
Gives one outcome that would cast doubt on the pipeline rather than on the robot.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: You expect a success rate near 0.8. About how many episodes give a 95 % half-width of 0.05? (integer)
